1. # View Design: mm::virt::identity_map
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers, this module is the **kernel lazy identity map**: a partial,
6. monotonically-growing set of physical pages that are reachable (identity-mapped)
7. through the kernel address space, plus a one-shot "is the mapper live yet?"
8. status. The only externally meaningful operation in scope, `identity_map_page`,
9. is an *idempotent side effect* — "make sure this physical page is reachable in
10. the kernel address space" — not a query returning data.
11. 
12. `ensure_pt` and `ensure_pte` are private sub-steps of that operation. Their
13. page-table / physical-address details are deliberately *not* part of this View
14. (callers explicitly do not observe them); they are specified at the page-table
15. structural level over their `Table` argument's own view, and connect back to the
16. module View only through the `mapped` set (see "Spec Transition Functions").
17. 
18. ---
19. 
20. ## View Struct
21. 
22. ```rust
23. /// Abstract state of the kernel lazy identity map.
24. ///
25. /// This is the caller-visible state behind the free functions in
26. /// `mm::virt::identity_map` (which operate over module-global statics, not a
27. /// `self` receiver). `identity_map_page` is specified as a transition on this
28. /// View; the private helpers refine it.
29. pub struct IdentityMapView {
30.     /// Whether `init` has published the kernel page directory.
31.     ///
32.     /// Before this is `true` (boot page tables still active), every
33.     /// `identity_map_page` call is a no-op success that leaves `mapped`
34.     /// unchanged. Callers are required to tolerate this pre-init no-op.
35.     pub initialized: bool,
36. 
37.     /// Page frame numbers currently reachable through the kernel identity map
38.     /// (the page's PTE is present). `frame == phys_addr / PAGE_SIZE`.
39.     ///
40.     /// A page-aligned physical address `p` is reachable iff
41.     /// `mapped.contains(p / PAGE_SIZE)`. The set only ever grows (mappings are
42.     /// never torn down by the in-scope functions).
43.     pub mapped: Set<nat>,
44. }
45. ```
46. 
47. Frame numbers (not byte addresses) are used so the set carries no implicit
48. page-alignment obligation; the `maps()` helper recovers the address-level query.
49. 
50. ---
51. 
52. ## Well-formedness Invariant
53. 
54. ```rust
55. impl IdentityMapView {
56.     /// Largest-valid-frame bound: a frame number is addressable iff it is
57.     /// strictly below this. Corresponds to the hardware `FrameNumber` range
58.     /// whose violation `ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page` report as
59.     /// `ErrorCode::BadAddress`. (= physical-address-space size / PAGE_SIZE.)
60.     pub open spec fn max_frames() -> nat;
61. 
62.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
63.         // Every reachable page denotes a valid physical frame. No partially
64.         // installed / out-of-range frame is ever recorded as mapped, mirroring
65.         // the all-or-nothing failure guarantee.
66.         forall|f: nat| #[trigger] self.mapped.contains(f) ==> f < Self::max_frames()
67.     }
68. }
69. ```
70. 
71. `inv()` is intentionally weak: pre-allocation of PDEs over `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)`
72. after `init` is a property of the *kernel page directory's* structural state, not
73. of the page-reachability set, so it is asserted in the helper specs over the
74. `Table` view rather than baked into this View's invariant.
75. 
76. ---
77. 
78. ## Spec Helpers (on the View, reusable in specs)
79. 
80. ```rust
81. impl IdentityMapView {
82.     /// Address-level reachability query: is the page covering `phys_addr`
83.     /// identity-mapped in the kernel address space?
84.     pub open spec fn maps(self, phys_addr: int) -> bool {
85.         self.mapped.contains((phys_addr / PAGE_SIZE) as nat)
86.     }
87. }
88. ```
89. 
90. ---
91. 
92. ## Spec Transition Functions
93. 
94. ### `identity_map_page` (external contract — the one callers see)
95. 
96. ```rust
97. impl IdentityMapView {
98.     /// Effect of identity-mapping the page with frame number `frame`.
99.     /// - Pre-init: no-op (callers must tolerate this).
100.     /// - Live: the frame becomes reachable. `Set::insert` is idempotent, so
101.     ///   re-mapping an already-mapped page is automatically a no-op success
102.     ///   (captures the "idempotent" caller expectation with no special case).
103.     pub open spec fn spec_identity_map_page(self, frame: nat) -> IdentityMapView {
104.         if self.initialized {
105.             IdentityMapView { mapped: self.mapped.insert(frame), ..self }
106.         } else {
107.             self
108.         }
109.     }
110. }
111. ```
112. 
113. Intended use on the exec function (`phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>`,
114. let `frame = phys_addr@ / PAGE_SIZE`):
115. 
116. - **Success** ⇒ `self@ == old(self)@.spec_identity_map_page(frame)` and
117.   `self@.maps(phys_addr@)` (map-on-success: the covering page is reachable).
118. - **Failure** ⇒ `self@ == old(self)@` (all-or-nothing: nothing is installed or
119.   consumed; `initialized` unchanged).
120. - `initialized` is never flipped by this function (frame condition: it only
121.   reads the global state).
122. 
123. ### `ensure_pte` (private sub-step — refines the `mapped` set)
124. 
125. `ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)` is the step that actually makes a page
126. reachable. Its post-state is expressed at the page-table level over its `pt`
127. argument's own view, and corresponds to inserting `phys_addr / PAGE_SIZE` into
128. `mapped`:
129. 
130. - **Success** ⇒ `pt@[pte_idx]` is present and identity-maps `phys_addr`
131.   (`frame == phys_addr / PAGE_SIZE`); idempotent if already present. This is the
132.   page-table witness for `self@.maps(phys_addr)` after `identity_map_page`.
133. - **Failure** (`InvalidArgument` bad read / `BadAddress` frame out of range,
134.   i.e. `frame >= max_frames()`) ⇒ `pt@` unchanged (no PTE written).
135. 
136. ### `ensure_pt` (private sub-step — structural precondition, *not* in `mapped`)
137. 
138. `ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx) -> usize` ensures a page table *exists* for `pde_idx`.
139. This is below the page-reachability abstraction and does not change `mapped`; it
140. is specified purely over the `pd` argument's `Table` view plus its return value:
141. 
142. - **Success** ⇒ `pd@[pde_idx]` is present afterwards, and the returned `usize` is
143.   the physical base of that page table (freshly allocated ⇒ all PTEs absent /
144.   zeroed, or the pre-existing one). Idempotent: a present PDE is returned without
145.   allocation.
146. - **Failure** (`InvalidArgument` / `OutOfMemory` no BSS slot / `BadAddress` PT
147.   frame out of range) ⇒ no PDE installed; `pd@` unchanged.
148. 
149. The returned physical address is internal plumbing (fed to `Table::from_address`
150. by `identity_map_page`); it never appears in any caller-facing clause, so it is
151. not modeled in the View.
152. 
153. ---
154. 
155. ## Design Rationale (per field, with substitution test)
156. 
157. | Field | Why it's needed | Substitution test |
158. |-------|-----------------|-------------------|
159. | `mapped: Set<nat>` | The whole point of the module: "which physical pages are reachable in kernel space." Used by `maps()`, `spec_identity_map_page`, and the map-on-success / idempotence ensures. | ✅ Any reimplementation (different paging scheme, different lazy strategy, eager mapping) still maintains *some* set of reachable pages. The concept is the resource itself, not a strategy. |
160. | `initialized: bool` | Callers are explicitly required to tolerate the pre-init no-op; the function's observable behavior differs across this boundary, so specs must name it. | ✅ Borderline but justified: the boot architecture (boot page tables → published kernel PD) is fundamental to the kernel, and callers *depend* on the no-op-before-ready behavior. Any rewrite still has a "mapper not live yet ⇒ no-op" phase. Modeled as an abstract `bool`, not the underlying `KERNEL_PD_PADDR == 0` static. |
161. 
162. Both fields use mathematical types (`Set`, `bool`, `nat`) and live entirely in
163. spec world; no `usize`, pointer, or flag-bit detail leaks in.
164. 
165. ---
166. 
167. ## Rejected Alternatives
168. 
169. 1. **`kernel_pd_paddr: int`, `kernel_cr3: int` fields** (mirroring the statics).
170.    Rejected: implementation-specific physical addresses. Callers never observe
171.    them; only the *fact* of initialization matters. Collapsed into the single
172.    `initialized: bool`. Fails the substitution test (a rewrite might not even use
173.    CR3 / a single PD root).
174. 
175. 2. **`pde_present: Set<nat>` / `page_tables: Map<nat, int>`** (per-PDE page-table
176.    allocation, base addresses). Rejected for the module View: the caller analysis
177.    states callers explicitly *don't care* whether a new page table was allocated
178.    vs reused, nor any page-table physical address. PDE presence is a structural
179.    fact of the kernel PD, specified locally over `ensure_pt`'s `Table` argument
180.    view, not promoted into the abstraction boundary. Fails substitution
181.    (page-directory/page-table structure is an x86 hardware strategy detail).
182. 
183. 3. **Return-address modeling for `ensure_pt`** (e.g., a field recording each
184.    PDE's PT base). Rejected: the `usize` is pure internal plumbing that "never
185.    surfaces to callers." Modeling it would be code-as-spec.
186. 
187. 4. **`mapped: Set<int>` of byte / page-aligned addresses** instead of frame
188.    numbers. Rejected: encoding page-alignment into set membership invites
189.    redundant alignment side-conditions in every clause. Frame numbers are the
190.    canonical page identity; the `maps(phys_addr)` helper recovers address-level
191.    queries when needed.
192. 
193. 5. **TLB-shootdown / TLB-validity state.** Rejected: not caller-observable; TLB
194.    invalidation is an internal correctness obligation of `ensure_pte`, not part
195.    of the page-reachability resource. A rewrite could batch or defer
196.    invalidation without changing the abstract contract.
197. 
198. 6. **PTE/PDE flag-bit fields (present, RW, user/supervisor, etc.).** Rejected:
199.    callers explicitly don't care about exact flag bits. "Reachable" (present +
200.    identity) is the only abstract property; the concrete flags are HOW, not WHAT.
201. 
202. 7. **A "monotone / append-only" history field.** Rejected: monotonicity (the
203.    in-scope functions never unmap) is a *property to prove across a transition*
204.    (`old(self)@.mapped.subset_of(self@.mapped)`), expressible from the existing
205.    `mapped` field, not a separate piece of state.
206.
